connector: Chapter 14 is the saddest chapter in the book. Lucy and Susan cannot sleep, so they follow Aslan into the moonlight. Read it slowly. Notice what Aslan chooses to do, and what it might show about the story’s big lesson. The story is not over yet.

a.raw: "cant you get to sleep either" said susan
a.fixed: "Can’t you get to sleep either?" said Susan.
a.why: Can’t starts the spoken words and joins can and not. The question mark goes inside the quotation mark. Susan is a name.

b.why: We starts the spoken words. The comma goes inside the quotation mark. The tag ends with a period.

glossary.m: the big lesson a story teaches, said as a full sentence
what a story is about, in a word or two, like loyalty or winter
the words characters say out loud in a story
the marks “ and ” that go around the exact words someone says
the part that tells who is talking, like said Lucy
the main part of a word that holds its meaning, like ject, which means throw
a part added to the front or the end of a word, like un- or -ed
telling the truth, even when it is hard

cards.title: World Notes: Stone Tables
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: Long ago, people in Ireland, Britain, France and many other places built real stone tables called dolmens.
A dolmen is a big flat stone set on top of standing stones. Many were built more than 5,000 years ago, and some are still standing.
Nobody knows exactly how such heavy stones were lifted. In the story, the Stone Table is very old, too, and the Deep Magic is written on it.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Chapter 14 is the saddest chapter in the book. Read it slowly, and notice what Aslan chooses to do.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: match ject words, fix dialogue mistakes, and find long words built from parts.
transcripts.guide2: Read Chapter 14. Then watch my video in Read Like a Writer.
transcripts.guide3: Today you draft your response on theme.

notes.wordParts: The root ject means throw. reject = throw back. inject = throw into. eject = throw out. project = throw forward.
notes.grammar: Quotation marks go around the exact words someone says. The first word gets a capital. The comma or period goes inside the closing mark: “Let him approach,” said Aslan.
notes.spelling: A long word is often a root with parts added. Find the root first: un + expect + ed = unexpected.
notes.wgrd: Aslan gives his own life so that Edmund can go free. This is strong proof for a theme about love or sacrifice.
vocab: someone who betrays the trust of their own side
to make up for a wrong you have done
giving up something precious for something or someone more important

mods.todo: Listen to Opti. Then tap the lens you will use today.
mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. In Chapter 14, notice what Aslan chooses to do. A choice like that can be strong proof for a theme. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. We couldn't sleep, said Lucy. We starts with a capital. The comma goes inside the quotation mark, and the tag, said Lucy, ends with a period. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Read the poem out loud. Say which kind it is, and two reasons why.
mods.script: [curious] Here's a short poem by Emily Dickinson. Read it out loud. Count the lines, and listen to the ends of the lines. Is it free verse, rhymed verse, a haiku, or a limerick? Answer out loud.

mods.todo: Tap a word, then tap what it means. Match all four words.
mods.script: Watch one match first. Interject. Inter means between, and ject means throw. To interject is to throw your words in while someone else is talking. That's my match! Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.

mods.todo: Tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all three words.
mods.script: Ever seen a face so serious that nobody dared to ask a question? Stern. Aslan's face was stern. Stern means very serious, and a little strict. Now tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all three.

mods.todo: Find each mistake. Tap Now check your thinking. Then tap every word that is wrong.
mods.script: Find the two mistakes. come here. said Dad. Come needs a capital, because it starts the spoken words. And that period should be a comma, inside the quotation mark. Read the four sentences, and tap Now check your thinking. Then fix the paragraph.

mods.todo: Read the rule. Tap every word built from a root with parts added.
mods.script: Root hunt! Lucy unlocked the door. Unlocked: un, lock, e d. Lock is the root, with parts on both ends. That one gets a tap! Read the rule. Then tap every word in the two sentences that is built from a root with parts added.

mods.todo: Read Chapter 14 in your book. Then try the Truth Watch below.
mods.script: Read Chapter 14 in your book, with your lens in mind. It is the saddest chapter in the book, and something very sad happens to Aslan. Read it slowly, and take a break if you need one. It is okay to feel sad. The story is not over yet. Then try the Truth Watch, and watch my video in the Read Like a Writer box.

mods.label: Opti shows you how
mods.script: Let's try all three parts with part of a sentence from Chapter 14. They kissed his mane and his nose and his paws and his great, sad eyes. Part one, read like a reader. Lucy and Susan love Aslan, and they are saying goodbye. Part two, read like a writer. It's a list joined by and. The last one, his great, sad eyes, is the longest, so the list ends slowly. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: I hugged my dog's ears and his nose and his paws and his warm, sleepy head. Now it's your turn with the Witch's list of names. Write one sentence in each box.

mods.todo: Answer each question in full sentences. Use details from the book.
mods.script: Three questions, in full sentences. One, what happens at the Stone Table, in order. Two, how Lucy and Susan show they are loyal. Three, how Chapter 14 is proof for your theme.

mods.todo: Draft your response: your theme, and proof from two parts of the story.
mods.script: Today you draft. Clara said her theme as a full sentence. Then she gave proof from the beginning and the middle of the story. Write your draft the same way.

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: When Peter says Aslan will be at the battle, Aslan says, “I can give you no promise of that.”
items.why: He will not make a promise he may not keep.

items.t: Lucy tells Susan she has a horrible feeling, and Susan says she has the same feeling.
items.why: They both say how they really feel.

items.t: When the girls ask what is wrong, Aslan tells them, “I am sad and lonely.”
items.why: He tells them the truth about his feelings.
